why: The new absorption-law logic in RexSimplify is non-trivial boolean rewriting run unconditionally in a hot simplification path with no benchmark (correctness, performance), and it visibly changes plan/satisfiability output across several unrelated tests including materialized-view substitution, so backward-compat impact and test coverage (cap threshold, multi-sibling cases) need a focused look.

Complex, multi-subsystem change (parser, validator, metadata, optimizer rules, codegen) extending OFFSET to arbitrary expressions: correctness, tests, backward_compat, error_model, surprising_behavior and spec_conformance are labeled 2 due to rounding/negative-offset validation changes, new rule logic in SortUnionTransposeRule/EnumerableMergeUnionRule, and deviation from SQL:2008's literal-only OFFSET.

This is a small, self-contained bug-fix to a planner rule's correctness condition, so `correctness` is the core axis to scrutinize (is the guard condition precise, does it handle nullable/false emptiness correctly, are there other empty-input edge cases like GROUPING SETS or non-empty group sets with empty input on the join side); other axes only need a glance since docs/comments/tests are all included in the diff and are small.

The new Collect.isValid contains non-trivial branching logic over MAP/ARRAY/MULTISET shapes (correctness) with new failure messages (error_model) but lacks javadoc explaining the invariant it enforces (doc_comments); it's a small, cohesive change a single reviewer can cover.

correctness is the core of this bugfix (verify the symmetric getFunctionKind() mapping actually fixes the asymmetry without introducing new false matches, and check edge cases like operators whose kind maps differently); backward_compat matters since loosening the filter could make previously-rejected ambiguous overloads now resolve differently for existing users.

The PR rewrites the string-literal escaping algorithm for Pig Latin, so correctness and spec_conformance (does it now match Pig's actual backslash-escaping rules, including untested control chars) are central, tests must be checked for edge-case coverage, and security matters because this is quoting/escaping logic feeding a generated script from potentially untrusted values.

New non-trivial join algorithm (paper implementation with NaN/type restrictions, null handling, key normalization) makes correctness and spec/paper-conformance central; cost model and claimed 2NlogN complexity owe a performance check; tests/backward_compat get a glance since new tests are included but the algorithm's edge cases (nulls, mixed types, three-plus predicates) need scrutiny.

correctness is central since the new condition (skip push-down when OFFSET/FETCH already set) needs checking for edge cases like partial offset-only or fetch-only, and combined ORDER BY+OFFSET/FETCH already on outer query; backward_compat is flagged because this changes existing query rewrite behavior (previously OFFSET/FETCH from outer ORDER BY could overwrite inner select's, now it won't) which could alter output for existing queries relying on old behavior.

Non-trivial recursive identifier-expansion logic for common columns (NATURAL/USING joins) in ORDER BY, with COALESCE for FULL JOIN and alias-stripping in AggChecker, needs a careful correctness/spec-conformance check; changing public/protected method signatures (expandCommonColumn now on SqlValidatorImpl with new overload) touches backward compatibility.

tests: the PR re-enables tests by updating expected plan/selectivity to match current output, so a reviewer must verify the new expected values (semi-join plan, 1.0/DEPT_SIZE) are actually correct rather than just codifying a possibly-wrong current behavior; correctness: same concern applies to whether the updated plan and selectivity calculation are genuinely right, not just 'whatever the optimizer currently emits'.

This is a small, focused bug fix in SqlValidatorImpl's checkRollUpInSelectList requiring careful correctness review (expansion logic, cast to Expander/SelectScope, unmodeled edge cases like natural joins with rollup columns) since it's non-trivial validator logic; tests exist but only cover the happy path, not the rollup interaction the fix targets.

This is a broad, risky change: it silently alters default generated-SQL/CQL/query output (backslash escaping, identifier quoting) across many dialects and adapters, so security, backward_compat, surprising_behavior, correctness and spec_conformance (unverified per-dialect escape rules) all get 2, plus tests and user_docs given the scope and new system property.

build_ci is central (Gradle toolchain, CI matrix, foojay resolver version pin, ErrorProne/Checker overrides) and correctness needs a careful check (does --release 8 plus toolchain actually guarantee JDK8 API-only bytecode across all subprojects, JavaExec/annotation-processor toolchains, and the auto-download=false interaction); other axes are only lightly touched.

Non-trivial lazy-init/buffer/seek logic in getLo(), reset(), and the new skip() (boundary math, overflow clamp, silent mark() failure) drives correctness/error_model/surprising_behavior/concurrency/spec_conformance to 2; the explicit performance claim, the observable behavior change to a public class (backward_compat), and the large new test surface plus new/changed javadoc contracts warrant a focused pass on tests, doc_comments, performance and contradictions.

correctness and contradictions are 2 because several newly-added entries carry gettext 'fuzzy' flags with mismatched/copy-pasted translations (e.g. connectExecutor msgid mapped to an unrelated SSL-context msgstr) that contradict the PR's own claim that only exact msgid matches were filled; surprising_behavior is 2 since such fuzzy/mismatched strings could surface as wrong text to Italian users if compiled in.

This is a mechanical, self-contained addition of 436 alias mappings across 13 files, so correctness (right old-slug→new-page mapping, no duplicate aliases that could break the Hugo build) is the main risk a focused reviewer must verify; other axes only warrant a glance (change_description/tests/build_ci for the build-and-link-check claim, contradictions for mapping-vs-content mismatches).

build_ci and correctness are central since this is a CI/workflow logic rewrite with intricate conditionals (fallback report, matrix flags, gating); security is flagged for committing a Codecov token into a public repo as a fork-PR fallback; user_value is flagged to weigh the token-commit design and manual_trigger approach against simpler alternatives (e.g. tokenless uploads).

Correctness is the core of this small fix (does reordering closed=true fully resolve the deadlock/exception on flush without introducing re-entrancy or double-close issues), and tests is required since a bug fix must add a regression test proving the original failure and the fix.

correctness is 2 because the epoch-bump/ordering logic in receiveParameterStatus and the skip-condition in processResults are subtle and version-dependent; spec_conformance is 2 because the whole feature hinges on correctly interpreting PostgreSQL 18's GUC_REPORT behavior for search_path.

This is a docs-only changelog PR, so user_docs (accuracy of the release notes themselves) is the core check, and contradictions matters because entries cite PR numbers repeatedly (e.g. #4014 for four different fixes) and duplicate content across CHANGELOG.md and the new release-note file that must stay consistent.

This is a security fix (GHSA) changing channel-binding negotiation logic, so security, correctness, error_model, and spec_conformance (RFC 5929/SCRAM) need focused review; the behavior change (silent downgrade -> hard fail) makes backward_compat, surprising_behavior, and test coverage of edge cases equally important to check.

The description claims the checkNotEmpty guard and new tests cover six entry points (toTimestamp, toDate, toLocalDate, toLocalDateTime, toOffsetDateTime, toOffsetTime), but the +6-line diff only patches one code location and the two new tests only exercise toTimestamp, so tests, correctness, contradictions, and change_description all need a focused check to confirm the fix's actual scope matches its claims.

Routine automated dependency bump pinning a new actions/checkout SHA across many workflow files; only build_ci (verify SHA matches v6.1.0 tag and pin format is consistent) merits a quick glance, with security touched superficially since it's a third-party action pin.

This is a test-only addition referencing Issue #4333, so the core question is whether the test is well-designed and actually exercises/fails-on the reported bug (tests, correctness); the empty description leaves the link to the issue and rationale unstated (change_description).

This is a security-critical rewrite of the wire-protocol reader (untrusted-input length validation, bounded buffer growth, GSS packet caps), so security, correctness, and spec_conformance need close scrutiny against the PostgreSQL/libpq limits it claims to mirror; the new explicit error paths, truncation behavior, and 'mark connection broken' changes alter observable behavior for existing users, so error_model, backward_compat, and surprising_behavior are also owed a focused look, backed by the extensive new tests.

This is a build tooling bump (Gradle 9.6.1, AGP 9.3.0) so build_ci is the core axis to verify (checksum correctness, AGP 9.x compatibility with existing config, min JDK requirements); correctness gets a light check on the wrapper script comment edits (cosmetic, low risk).

This is a focused, non-trivial bug-fix in generics/wildcard-capture handling (captured type wildcard annotation restoration), so `correctness` is the central axis given the subtle javac Type mutation logic (cloning captured types, sharing wildcards) and edge cases across testDirect/testWithVar/self paths; other axes only warrant a glance since the change is well-tested and internal to a single cohesive area.

correctness and spec_conformance are central since the PR hand-crafts detached javac TypeVar/CapturedType copies to satisfy identity/baseType invariants while implementing unbound-wildcard and F-bounded-cycle semantics; tests and doc_comments get 2 because the new unit tests and extensive new javadoc must actually prove/describe these subtle aliasing and cycle-detection guarantees.

This is a small, cohesive bug fix (Map→SetMultimap) that a single reviewer can cover; correctness is the key axis since it's the entire point of the fix (verify the multimap change actually resolves the BiConsumer multi-bound issue and no callers still assume single-value semantics), with a light glance at tests/backward_compat/contradictions given the public method's return type changed and a regression test was added.

correctness=2 for the intricate new type-matching/fallback logic for anonymous diamond classes (getMatchingInstantiatedType, hasInferredClassTypeArguments, strict-supertype conservatism); other axes get at most a glance since the change is contained to generics inference logic with accompanying tests and no public API, security, or build surface touched.

New 943-line spec-implementing checker with dense tree-walking edge cases owes a hard correctness/spec_conformance/error_model pass, and the description's claim of SUGGESTION severity contradicts the code's WARNING severity (contradictions/backward_compat/surprising_behavior); the new check plus its flags need docs, changelog, and scrutiny of its large test suite (user_docs, change_description, tests, doc_comments, user_value).

Core logic is intricate raw-array/generic-method-reference resolution requiring deep correctness, spec_conformance, and surprising_behavior scrutiny; the diff also silently bundles a substantial unbound-method-reference qualifier resolution refactor and public API signature change (getMemberReferenceMethodType) not mentioned in the title/description, raising change_description, contradictions, doc_comments, and backward_compat concerns.

This is a small, mechanical model addition (registering takeWhile as filter-like across three stream APIs) with no accompanying tests, so `tests` is the clear required check; `correctness` is required since the semantic equivalence of takeWhile to filter for nullability purposes (it truncates rather than just excludes, but per-element nullability propagation should still match) deserves a focused look.

This is a small CI-only workflow change, so build_ci is mandated and correctness of the concurrency-group expression/merge_group trigger logic (e.g. behavior on push to master vs PR vs merge queue) deserves a focused check; everything else is untouched.

This is a CI/dependency-policy change (build_ci) whose embedded TOML/JSON-parsing validation script and the intricate matchJsonata/allowedVersions rules carry non-trivial correctness risk, an unpinned renovate/renovate:latest Docker pull is a deliberate but debatable security trade-off, and the very long, precise description invites checking for contradictions between stated rationale and actual rule behavior (e.g. schedule inheritance across Error Prone rules).

Core risk is in the intricate wildcard-capture/type-substitution logic touching object-mutation and cycle-guard invariants (correctness, spec_conformance, surprising_behavior), which the added regression tests and updated internal Javadoc must be checked to actually cover and accurately describe (tests, doc_comments).

Core logic changes to wildcard/capture upper-bound resolution are non-trivial and spec-driven (correctness, spec_conformance), require solid regression tests (tests), and are accompanied by extensive rewritten javadoc/description that must stay consistent with the tricky new code (doc_comments, contradictions); the added capture-conversion calls sit in the type-checking hot path with no benchmark (performance).
